subject: Runtime event-surface exemption for EdgeCache vendor — product & security sign-off needed
messages:
From: Sean Taylor <sean.taylor@edgecache.io>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: limited runtime event surface exemption for EdgeCache integration

Hi Karthik —

Thanks again for the demo last week. EdgeCache is ready to move forward with a pilot using Redwood Dedicated for our CDN-integrated inference cache. Our procurement team has one ask while legal finalizes the SOW: we need a narrow DPA carveout that allows EdgeCache to receive a small set of runtime event signals (cache hits/misses, anonymized latency bucketing, and per-shard error counts) for usage-based analytics.

Key constraints we proposed:
- Events are aggregated at 1-minute buckets, no user identifiers, IPs redacted before export.
- TTL on exported events: 30 days.
- Data used strictly for operational analytics and cache optimization; no model training.

I attached the SOW draft (EdgeCache-SOW_v3.pdf) and a proposed event mapping (runtime-event-mapping.xlsx). Can you route to your product/security folks for a quick signoff or identify which fields are blockers?

Happy to hop on a call — Sean
--
Sean Taylor
Head of Partnerships, EdgeCache
sean.taylor@edgecache.io
+1 (415) 555-0187

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Sean Taylor <sean.taylor@edgecache.io>
Date: 2026-09-20T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: limited runtime event surface exemption for EdgeCache integration

Grace / Hannah —

Looping you in on a vendor ask that touches both product and security. EdgeCache wants a narrowly scoped export of aggregated runtime events to support cache analytics. The ask explicitly disallows model training, and they propose 30-day TTL + IP redaction.

Questions from my side for product/security:
1) Is per-shard error counts + minute-aggregates acceptable from a telemetry/data-use policy perspective?
2) Do we need explicit language disallowing use for feature engineering or training, or is the current clause sufficient?
3) Any operational constraints for Dedicated customers that would change how we batch or anonymize these exports?

Hannah — if legal wants to redline to our standard DPA carveouts, can you provide a short list of must-have language? Grace / Aditya — product and runtime implications would be helpful before I reply to Sean. Prefer to keep this scoped and not open a broad subprocessor exception.

Thanks — Karthik

On Sep 20, 2026, at 9:12 AM, Sean Taylor <sean.taylor@edgecache.io> wrote:

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Sean Taylor <sean.taylor@edgecache.io>, legal@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-21T08:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: limited runtime event surface exemption for EdgeCache integration

Thanks for the ping. I attached a quick redline to the DPA (redline-dpa.docx) with recommended language that: 1) explicitly forbids training and feature extraction, 2) defines the exported telemetry fields by name, and 3) requires a 30-day retention maximum with audit rights for Redwood.

Concise notes:
- "No training" language should be explicit and include a clause forbidding downstream model ingestion or feature store retention.
- Define the event set as: minute_bucketed_cache_hits, minute_bucketed_cache_misses, latency_p50_p95_buckets, shard_error_count. Any other fields must be scoped via written approval.
- Require HMAC-signed delivery endpoint or equivalent transport controls if they request push delivery; pull via secure API is preferred.

Grace/Product: the redline includes a clause that requires us to preserve the ability to disable exports per-customer in case of behavioral or privacy issues. Is that acceptable operationally? Aditya, can you confirm whether we can implement a per-customer kill switch and ensure IP redaction happens before export?

Hannah
--
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Counsel, Data & Privacy
Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Sean Taylor <sean.taylor@edgecache.io>
Date: 2026-09-22T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: limited runtime event surface exemption for EdgeCache integration

Karthik / Hannah / Aditya —

Quick operational reply after syncing with Aditya's runtime team. Summary: we can support the proposed minute-aggregates and the listed event types without changing the serving runtime behavior. Notes and small asks:

- Implementation: we will add an export pipeline that consumes internal aggregations (1-min buckets) after KV cache reconciliation. IPs and any PII will be redacted prior to placement in the export queue. We will not expose request-level identifiers.
- Kill switch: feasible. We'll expose a per-customer toggle in Console (Default: off for pilot until contract executed).
- Latency buckets: p50/p95 are trivial; we prefer fixed bucket definitions (0-10ms, 10-50ms, 50-200ms, >200ms) — please confirm.
- Transport: prefer pull from EdgeCache over HTTPS with mTLS or a secured S3 push with server-side encryption; HMAC-signed push endpoints are acceptable but require additional support.

One product policy question for Hannah: do we need to require a specific audit cadence or log retention for EdgeCache to demonstrate compliance with the "no training" commitment? Hannah, if you can propose language, we'll include it in the SOW.

Assuming Hannah's redline is accepted, I can sign off from product on the technical approach and we can move the SOW to procurement.

Grace
--
Grace O'Connor
Director, Product Management — Inference Platform
grace_oconnor@redwood.com

Status: awaiting Hannah's final redline merge and confirmation on audit cadence; product has agreed operationally pending exact bucket defs and transport method. Next step: Karthik to confirm transport preferences with EdgeCache and share finalized redline for countersignature.
